text:
jordan: Heads-up — noticed a surge of tenant-triggered SLO alerts last night. Looks like one tenant's retry storm caused a huge fanout and spiked notify costs.
maya: Ugh. Which SLOs fired? Was it error-rate or latency thresholds?
jordan: Mostly p50 latency and an error-rate alert cascade. The console bubbled both. Attached snippet from alert log: ```tenant=acme, rule=route_latency_p50, users=1200, fanout=350```
samira: Is the console's notify fanout honoring per-tenant silent windows / backoff? We added a soft-quarantine feature last quarter but not sure it's wired into the notify pipeline.
chris: Not wired. Console currently emits a notify_intent event to the routing API; routing does fanout. We considered adding attenuation hints in the intent payload but never finalized the API.
maya: So the product path is: console SLO editor -> notify_intent API -> routing service -> fanout. We need a short-term mitigator and a longer-term contract change.
jordan: Short-term: can routing apply a simple per-tenant rateproof cap for alerts (max N warns per minute) and a cooldown if fanout > X? That would cut costs and noise.
samira: Yes, + sampling for noisy tenants. We should surface in console when a tenant is being sampled/attenuated so users understand missed alerts. UI banner: "Attenuation applied — 40% of notifications sampled".
chris: Implementation note: we can add fields to notify_intent: `attenuation_mode` and `attenuation_factor`. Routing can honor them or override with `override_reason`. Backwards compatible — default = null (no attenuation).
maya: That API change sounds fine but needs api-spec update + console preview. Who owns the spec? @chris?
chris: I'll draft the openapi patch. Also need a telemetry event: `notify.attenuation_applied` with keys {tenant, rule, factor, reason}. That will help postmortem.
jordan: Ops asks for a fallback: if routing sees > 70% fanout increase in 5m, automatically engage system attenuation even without console hint. Should be opt-out per org.
samira: Agree. We also need an acceptance test in the deploy pipeline that simulates noisy tenant signal and asserts attenuation kicks in and console shows banner.
chris: I'll add a test to eng-platform/integration: `attenuation_flow_test`. Will require a small shim to fake notify backends.
maya: UX: in SLO editor show an "Alerting footprint" preview: estimated avg fanout, worst-case fanout, and cost delta for tiers. That would help teams tune thresholds.
jordan: Nice. Action items: 1) chris drafts API + telemetry (PR this week). 2) samira wires console banner + preview copy. 3) chris adds integration test. 4) ops adds emergency attenuation hook.
samira: I'll own the banner and the preview UX copy. Quick copy idea: "To reduce noisy alerts, notifications may be sampled. Learn more" with link to runbook.
chris: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/routing/pulls/248 — WIP. Adds `attenuation_factor` field. PTAL.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: routing/attenuation-service v0.4.3 -> staging at 03:10 UTC
jordan: Also let's add a per-tenant daily alert budget visible in console (simple counter). Not to block critical alerts but to surface heavy consumers.
maya: Strong +1. That helps CS conversations.
samira: Will sketch dashboard tiles for daily budget + last attenuation events.
jordan: Cool. If no objections I'll spin up a small RFC doc and schedule a 30m sync tomorrow.
maya: +1 from me. Sync invite when you have the RFC.
chris: will post API draft in #eng-platform when PR is ready.
jordan: Thanks all.
ops-bot: incident-note: noise-mitigation planned; alerting impact expected <5% for critical SLOs.
